source.author: lucan
source.text: Ut primum remis actum mare propulit omne Classis onus, densis fremuit niger imbribus Auster In sua regna furens: tentatum classibus aequor Turbine defendit, longeque a Syrtibus undas Egit, et illato confregit litore pontum.
source.text_original: Ut primum remis actum mare propulit omne / Classis onus, densis fremuit niger imbribus Auster / In sua regna furens: tentatum classibus aequor / Turbine defendit, longeque a Syrtibus undas / Egit, et illato confregit litore pontum.
source.text_english: As soon as the sea, driven by oars, had borne forth the whole burden of the fleet, black Auster roared, raging in its own realm, with thick showers: the storm held off the sea, though assailed by fleets, by its whirlwind, and drove the waves far from the Syrtes, and with the shore thrust upon it shattered the sea.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: at Iuno Argolicas pariter Macetumque per urbes spargit inexpertos temptare parentibus austros Aesoniden; iam stare ratem remisque superbam poscere quos revehat rebusque in saecula tollat.
reuse.text_original: at Iuno Argolicas pariter Macetumque per urbes / spargit inexpertos temptare parentibus austros / Aesoniden; iam stare ratem remisque superbam / poscere quos revehat rebusque in saecula tollat.
reuse.text_english: But Juno, through the Argive cities and the cities of the Macedonians alike, spreads the word that Aeison’s son is to try winds untested by his father; already the ship stands and, proud of its oars, asks for those whom it may carry back and raise by its deeds to the ages.
